bull.b: Sustained revenue expansion indicates increasing utilization of Soluna’s renewable-powered infrastructure and improving commercial traction. Five consecutive quarters of sequential growth provide a stronger foundation for scaling operations, attracting customers, and converting capacity investments into future recurring revenue.

A large development pipeline combined with preserved interconnection capacity supports Soluna’s ability to expand computing infrastructure where power availability is constrained. This positioning can improve execution prospects for future AI and hosting projects and strengthen its renewable-power advantage.

Owning generation assets while operating data centers gives Soluna greater control over power supply and site economics. The expanded Bitdeer relationship also validates its co-mining model, broadens monetization of renewable capacity, and supports scalable infrastructure utilization.

bear.b: Very low gross margins and deeply negative earnings show that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability. Continued operating losses limit internally funded expansion, increase dependence on capital markets, and leave the business vulnerable if project ramp-up takes longer than planned.

The expanded authorization materially increases Soluna’s ability to raise equity, but it also creates a durable dilution risk for existing shareholders. Reliance on new shares may be necessary to fund development, yet can reduce per-share ownership and signal that internal cash generation remains insufficient.

The decline in proprietary mining revenue demonstrates pressure on an established monetization stream and highlights the sensitivity of current operations to mining economics. Although hosting is expanding, the transition may require time to offset weaker direct mining contribution and support consolidated margins.
